Rep. Nancy Mace questions official finances and highlights legislation for women’s safety
U.S. Representative Nancy Mace used her social media platform on October 14-15 to question potential financial discrepancies among officials and emphasize new legislative measures focused on protecting women and children.
Rep. Nancy Mace, currently serving as the U.S. Representative for South Carolina’s 1st district, posted a series of statements on her social media account between October 14 and 15, 2026, addressing government accountability and legislative efforts to protect women and children.
On October 14, Mace questioned the financial status of public officials by stating, "The $30 million net worth on a $174,000 salary might be worth investigating too. Just saying."
Later that evening, she highlighted recent legislative actions aimed at safeguarding vulnerable populations: "Women and children deserve to be safe. For too long, Washington has left them to fend for themselves. We got to work and have introduced more than 20 bills to protect women and children, hold predators accountable and give survivors their power back. Speak Your Truth Act https://t.co/aBVpATyPyG".
On October 15, Mace commented on public sentiment regarding fairness in government: "Americans are tired of double standards. They want accountability. Every small win is a step toward the government they deserve."
Mace has represented South Carolina's 1st District in Congress since replacing Joe Cunningham in 2021 and previously served in the South Carolina House of Representatives from 2018 to 2020. Born in Fort Bragg, North Carolina, in 1977, she currently resides in Charleston and graduated from The Citadel with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1999.
